Chewy Pumpkin Spice Cookies

In: autumn, cakes + cookies + sweets, desserts, recipes, season, vegetarian
Jump to Recipe
Print Recipe

These soft, chewy Pumpkin Spice Cookies are the perfect fall treat! Made with real pumpkin and cozy spices, they’re delicious served with hot cider or chai. Plus, they’ll make your house smell amazing while they’re cooking in the oven!

I’ve really been trying to step up my baking game over the past year or so, and my focus has been on cookies. I tested these Cornbread Cookies and these Thanksgiving Cookies a bajillion times before posting, and these Pumpkin Spice Cookies are no different!

It’s scary posting a baking recipe online because no matter how many times you test it, no matter how detailed you try to write the instructions, there are a lot of variables in your readers’ kitchens that you can’t control. For example, ovens can run hot or cold, with airflow and heat conduction varying wildly. Then there’s also things like barometric pressure, altitude, the ambient temperature of one’s kitchen (just to name a few) that can muck up a recipe. Still, I had a few of my friends test this recipe for me to make sure it would work out in their kitchens (and it does!). (Shout out to Kat and Julia!)

Lastly, this was intended to be a snickerdoodle recipe, but as the recipe morphed over the months of testing, I wasn’t sure if it still merited that title. Most snickerdoodles I’ve had in my life have leaned toward soft instead of chewy, but these cookies are CHEWY. (Which is my favorite type of cookie!) So I decided to omit “snickerdoodle” from the title. But let me know if in the comments if you agree with my assessment! Cheers!

For more cozy desserts, try my Cornbread Cookies or my Chocolate Chip Banana Bread! These cookies would also be super tasty served with my Banana Bread Latte.

Chewy Pumpkin Spice Cookies

These soft, chewy Pumpkin Spice Cookies are the perfect fall treat! Made with real pumpkin and cozy spices, they're perfect served with hot cider or chai!
Course Cookies, Dessert
Keyword brown sugar, pumpkin, pumpkin pie spice, pumpkin spice, vanilla
Prep Time 20 minutes minutes
Cook Time 10 minutes minutes
Chilling Time 1 hour hour
Servings 18 Cookies
Calories 134kcal

Ingredients

Wet Ingredients

  • 113 g Unsalted Butter 1/2 cup, at room temperature
  • 106 g Brown Sugar 1/2 cup, tightly packed
  • 66 g Granulated Sugar 1/3 cup
  • 1 Egg Yolk
  • 73 g Pumpkin Purée, Patted Dry 1/3 cup
  • 1 Tsp Vanilla Extract

Dry Ingredients

  • 160 g All-Purpose Flour 1 1/3 cups
  • 1/2 Tsp Cinnamon
  • 1 Tsp Pumpkin Pie Spice
  • 1/4 Tsp Salt
  • 1/2 Tsp Baking Soda
  • 1/2 Tsp Cream of Tartar

Sugar Coating

  • 1 Tsp Cinnamon
  • 66 g Sugar 1/3 cup

Instructions

  • Cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3-4 minutes.
  • Measure out the pumpkin purée. Gently press a paper towel into the pumpkin, soaking up any excess liquid. (Slowly peeling off the paper towel from the pumpkin should help prevent it from sticking to the towel.)
  • Then, add in the pumpkin purée, egg yolk, and vanilla to the butter and sugar, and mix again until evenly combined. Scrape the sides of the bowl with a spatula to make sure no pieces of butter are left behind, and mix again to combine.
  • In another bowl, whisk together the flour, cinnamon, pumpkin pie spice, salt, cream of tartar, and baking soda.
  • Pour the dry ingredients into the mixing bowl with the wet ingredients and gently mix until JUST combined. Towards the end of mixing, the dough will be very crumbly and difficult to mix.
  • Put the bowl of cookie dough in the refrigerator, covered, for AT LEAST 1 hour.
  • When ready to cook, preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
  • Using a 1 and a 1/2 inch cookie scoop, scoop out the cookie dough into even portions, then use your hands to shape the dough into balls. You should have about 18 cookie dough balls.
  • Sprinkle the sugar and cinnamon on a plate, then take a cookie dough ball and roll it in the mixture until coated. Repeat until you've coated all of the cookie dough.
  • Bake about 7-8 cookies at a time on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, at 375 degrees for 9-10 minutes. When done, allow cookies to cool on the same baking sheet for at least 5 minutes before transferring to a cooling rack.
  • When baking the next batch of cookies, be sure to use a new, room temperature baking sheet (instead of the hot one that just came out of the oven).
  • Enjoy!

Notes

  • Baking disclaimer: From 2025 on, I will be posting ALL of my baking recipes in grams. I will still provide Imperial, volume measurements in the notes, but I HIGHLY recommend purchasing a kitchen scale. I have this one from KitchenAid (affiliate link) and it’s super, super easy to use. Baking with a scale is more accurate and much easier.

Chewy Pumpkin Spice Cookies FAQs

Can I make these cookies ahead of time?

Yes! If making these cookies ahead of time, store them in the freezer after rolling them + coating them in sugar until ready to bake. Be sure to store them in a freezer-safe container to prevent freezer burn. Also, you may need to add 1-2 minutes to the baking time if cooking from frozen.

Are these Pumpkin Spice Cookies the same as snickerdoodles?

While these cookies contain cream of tartar and are coated in cinnamon sugar, I’m not sure if they totally qualify as snickerdoodles. As I wrote in the main post body, you’ll have to let me know in the comments if you agree with me or not! :)

Are these Chewy Pumpkin Spice Cookies made with pumpkin purée?

Yes, they are! The pumpkin purée helps boost the autumnal, pumpkin-y flavor. If you have leftover pumpkin purée, try my Pumpkin Spice Syrup! It’s perfect for coffee, pancakes, and ice cream sundaes!

Do I really have to pat the pumpkin purée dry?

Yes, you do! Patting the pumpkin dry ensures that no extra liquid gets into the cookie batter, which messes with the texture. So don’t skip this step!
